title: Commitment-variant experiments and enterprise SQ response template
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Run a set of product experiments to determine optimal commitment/ burst/ autoscaling packaging for Dedicated capacity customers and produce a canonical Security Questionnaire (SQ) response template for sales and CSMs. Focus areas: reserved GPU tiers, burst credits, autoscaling policies & SLAs, and mapping those to contract language and answers in common enterprise SQs.
background: Sales and Solutions Engineering frequently encounter inconsistent asks for: committed GPU reservations, short-term burst capacity, and autoscale behavior under spikes. Current proposals in engineering and pricing are fragmented across decks. We need a coordinated set of experiments to validate buyer price sensitivity, preferred commitment length, and the operational constraints that must be reflected in SLAs and SQ responses.
goals: Quantify willingness to pay for 3 commitment variants: monthly commit, 12-month commit, and convertible commit (commit with flexible burst credits)
Define 2 burst product primitives (pre-purchased credits & transient burst with overage pricing) and measure usage patterns
Codify autoscaling semantics customers expect and map to SLA language (99.9 vs 99.95 for latency and availability)
Produce an enterprise-ready SQ response template (controls, KMS/HSM, network isolation, audit logs) that maps to each packaging variant
Deliver clear metrics and go/no-go criteria for a minimal price catalog for GA in release dedicated-pricing-2026.04
success_metrics: Successful A/B tests with at least 20 paying pilots per cohort
Observed ARPA lift >= 18% for 12-month commit vs monthly commit in pilots
Burst usage median < 15% of committed capacity among participating accounts (to avoid unbounded costs)
Sales cycle time for Dedicated deals decreases by 10% when SQ template is used
Internal alignment signoff from legal, security, and engineering on SQ template
experiment_plan: Variant A — Monthly Commit: baseline per-GPU-hour rate with optional on-demand burst pricing (overage per GPU-hour). Offer a small discount for pre-paid monthly commitment.
Variant B — 12-Month Commit: discounted reserved rate with limited burst credits included (e.g., 20% of monthly commit per month). Provide rollback/cooldown policy and upgrade path.

Variant C — Convertible Commit: shorter initial commit (3 months) with option to convert to 12-month at any time; higher unit price but includes larger burst pool and priority routing during contention.
Pilot cohort selection: 30 candidate accounts segmented by expected QPS pattern (steady, spiky, seasonal). Assign 10 accounts per variant using stratified sampling.

Instrumentation: per-account token cost, GPU-hour utilization, burst credit consumption, tail latency percentiles, error rates, and SLA breaches. Add tags for sales rep and CSM to link contract negotiation artifacts.
Billing & contract language: create templated addendum clauses for burst usage, autoscale behavior, and credits reconciliation. Work with Legal to preapprove EULA language for each variant.

SQ template: draft canonical answers for top 50 SQ queries (KMS, data residency, patching cadence, RBAC, audit logs, incident notifications) and tie them to packaging options (e.g., '12-month commit includes monthly audit export by default').
acceptance_criteria: Experiment runbook published and reviewed by Eng/Revenue/Legal
Pilot cohorts onboarded and telemetry dashboards (Console + GA4) show correct instrumentation within 7 days of onboarding
Security Questionnaire template drafted and security/legal feedback loop closed (<= 5 business days for major comments)
Pricing catalog artifacts (CSV + sample contract addendum) produced and stored in Drive with versioning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Burst usage could be concentrated on a few accounts and blow out cost. Mitigation: cap per-account burst consumption in pilots and use throttled routing; simulate worst-case costs before GA.
Risk: SLA promises tied to autoscale may not be achievable on certain hardware topologies. Mitigation: work with ENG to define hardware-compatible SLA tiers and fallback model variants for spillover.
Risk: Sales rejects rigid commitment options. Mitigation: keep Convertible Commit as flexible alternative and allow negotiated credits in pilot stage.
Risk: SQ answers expose gaps in compliance posture. Mitigation: include security/infra owners in weekly reviews and gate final template on explicit signoff
notes: Initial pricing hypotheses: MSRP per-GPU-hour at current run-rate, show 10-20% discount bump for 12-month; Convertible at +5% to monthly but with priority routing value prop.
We should model unit economics with our current batching/caching assumptions; low-latency customers may not tolerate aggressive batching discounts.
Consider optional add-on: dedicated egress/private-link for compliance customers priced separately in quote builder. This will be surfaced in SQ template as 'network isolation option'.
